policy: All five historical components jointly required; valid alternative research earns scientific quality independently. Original answers and v1 preserved.

source.title: Discrete coding of reward probability and uncertainty by dopamine neurons

reviews.reason: All five components match: uncertainty versus value, p=0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 plus two magnitudes and matched means, separate delay/phasic readouts, movement/history controls and a replicated intermediate-peaked prediction. No causal necessity or universal exact-entropy claim is made.

The fixed-magnitude certainty/intermediate probability grid, matched-value challenge, separate middle-delay and cue/outcome responses, movement/history/cue controls and inverted-U directional prediction jointly match the sealed later study. Operational deductions remain separate from the valid historical core.

The uncertainty/value question and separated delay/phasic readout match. The actual core includes only p=.25/.5/.75; exact p=0 and p=1 are optional and interchangeable with .10/.90. It therefore does not commit to the sealed intermediate-versus-certainty intervention/prediction, though its alternative curvature/value experiment earns quality credit. This is not a penalty for failing to guess the historical result.
No substantive answer: none of the five historical-direction components is present.

The question/mechanism and intermediate probability intervention are historically related. The design lacks a certain-reward anchor and matched-value test, selects neurons by significant RPE responses, and lacks an independently validated uncertainty readout. These critical selection/control failures prevent a qualified joint historical prediction.

All nominal historical topics are present, but the certain fixed-time anchor is altered by unmodeled timing/omission probes and the varying-magnitude variance prediction is misdefined. These critical control/readout-prediction defects prevent a qualified match.

The 0/.5/1 delay-peak topic is present, but cells are selected on reward-error responses and neither independent identity nor value/behavior/cue controls qualify the readout. A generic 50% peak is insufficient for the joint historical match.

The uncertainty-versus-value question and matched-mean manipulation are present. The main equal-mean series has its largest amount variance at p=.25, not a fixed-magnitude half-probability maximum, and the required cue/learned-contingency controls are absent. The joint validated historical readout and half-versus-endpoint prediction are not satisfied.

Question, probability grid, delay/phasic separation and intermediate-peak prediction are present. The plan deliberately fixes magnitude throughout and never proposes the required matched-expected-value distribution challenge. It supports a narrower curved probability association, not the complete sealed value-separated historical criterion.

Nominally all historical contrasts and the positive intermediate-peak hypothesis are supplied, with excellent independent distributional replication. However the explicit SURE-transient requirement rejects valid predicted-reward nonresponses and gates all interpretation on that response-selected preparation. This critical population/positive-control failure prevents a qualified readout/prediction; a negative sign itself is NOT the reason for the miss.

The chosen question and primary model concern monotonic prospective value versus event-only signaling, not uncertainty separated from value. No intermediate-peaked uncertainty prediction is tested. Five probabilities and separated epochs alone do not create a direction hit; the reversed expected-time control is an additional critical defect.

The probability/uncertainty topic and intermediate-peak contrast match. Response-based identity/replication selection, deferred rather than committed matched-value controls, and automatic rejection of late-only uncertainty signals prevent the full validated historical readout and prediction.
